items.title: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease
items.excerpt: DeepMind's next-generation DNA sequence model bridges single-cell biology and human genetics, predicting how genetic variants affect specific human cell types and cell states to help interpret disease risk.

history_match.title: AI agents run this automated biology lab that sequences DNA and more

items.title: Machine learning reveals how often fish schooling evolved—and repeatedly disappeared
items.excerpt: Cornell researchers used a text transformer on species descriptions plus computer vision and 3D reconstruction of fish photos/videos to classify 2,839 species, finding schooling evolved independently ~60 times and was lost ~320 times over 350 million years (PNAS).

items.title: AI-generated molecular fingerprints help identify existing compounds with therapeutic potential
items.excerpt: University of Pittsburgh's DRUG-GAN generative adversarial network produces molecular fingerprints that are matched against chemical databases, surfacing structurally novel existing compounds predicted to bind GPCRs and kinases (Science Advances).

items.title: AI-assisted atomic models reveal how protective shells regulate aluminum nanoparticle oxidation
items.excerpt: Tohoku University's MLP Copilot, an AI-agent framework that builds machine-learning interatomic potentials via ~80 active-learning rounds and 88,833 configurations, simulated how oxide shells gate aluminum nanoparticle oxidation and when they rupture (PNAS).

items.title: AI-designed metasurface could make cameras far more light-efficient
items.excerpt: A neural-network-assisted inverse-design search produced a nanoscale colour router that delivers substantially more light to an image sensor than conventional absorptive colour filters.

items.title: OpenAI's 'shepherds' affirm blockbuster physics result
items.excerpt: A committee led by Nobel laureate David Gross affirmed OpenAI's AI-generated proof of the existence of quantum Yang-Mills theory and released an explanation plus Lean formal verification on Nov 10, while noting they do not yet fully understand the proof; the mass-gap question remains open.

history_match.title: Dueling proofs from OpenAI and Anthropic astound scientists

items.title: Virtual fruit fly brains can play Doom and trade bitcoin
items.excerpt: After Janelia released a 166,000-neuron male fruit fly connectome, programmers loaded the wiring map into AI models and trained them to play Doom, trade bitcoin and solve Rubik's cubes; neuroscientists caution this is not an uploaded fly mind.

history_match.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”

items.title: AI toolbox accelerates bioreactor simulations by up to 10,000 times
items.excerpt: TU Graz's open-source CLARA toolbox uses unsupervised machine learning to cluster CFD data into 5-50 linked compartments, yielding reduced-order bioreactor models that run up to 10,000x faster while conserving mass and mixing effects (Chemical Engineering Science).

items.title: New AI model could help UN nuclear watchdog achieve near-perfect uranium enrichment assessment
items.excerpt: University of Sharjah researchers trained XGBoost, CatBoost and LightGBM on simulated gamma spectra to estimate U-235 enrichment and perfectly classify natural, low- and highly enriched uranium, pending tests under real inspection conditions (Annals of Nuclear Energy).

items.title: Preserving human involvement at the start of a creative task can improve AI-assisted outcomes
items.excerpt: Wharton's Hosanagar and Ahn had 285 students write stories with ChatGPT under three human-AI workflows; human-steered and flexible designs beat unaided writing on quality and satisfaction, while approval-only AI drafting produced worse stories (PNAS Nexus).

items.title: People project a specific racial identity onto artificial intelligence, study finds
items.excerpt: Across five studies (~2,400 participants in the U.S., India and Japan), people associated AI with Whiteness even without human features, which modestly raised AI's persuasiveness; AI described as trained on Black and Latino adults was assigned less demanding work (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, Purdue/Northwestern).

items.title: 'The first species we might be able to communicate with... might be a bird': An animal researcher explains how she decoded birdsong
items.excerpt: UC Berkeley ethologist Julie Elie explains how a decade of recordings, machine learning and behavioral experiments decoded zebra finch calls, and what AI contributed to understanding bird vocal communication.

history_match.title: AI model decodes the language cells use to communicate

items.title: Using Vibrations and AI, Future Robotic Missions Could Handle Buried Rocks Autonomously
items.excerpt: Virginia Tech researchers built a multilayer-perceptron model that estimates the burial depth of rocks from 11 vibration features, letting future lunar robots decide autonomously whether to clear or avoid obstacles (IEEE Sensors Journal).

items.title: New AI Models Are Turbo-Charging Protein Design
items.excerpt: GEN roundup of AI protein design efforts; notably Claude-designed miniprotein binders synthesized and tested by Adaptyv Bio and Twist showed a 27% hit rate (354 of 1,320) with binders for 14 of 15 targets.

items.title: QuEra, Harvard and Anthropic Use AI to Reduce Quantum Circuit Resource Requirements
items.excerpt: Claude paired with an automated evaluator designed circuits for eight quantum building blocks, cutting Toffoli/qubit costs (e.g. 12x for a Reed-Solomon decoder, 39x for a Gaussian function) and finding a new reversible modular inversion (arXiv:2610.22367); resource estimates only, not hardware runs.

history_match.title: Anthropic's Claude Designs Leaner Quantum Circuits, Reducing Resources Needed for Key Calculations

items.title: Researchers Explore Quantum Inspired AI Repair
items.excerpt: QDeep and ITMO's Tree-Ising makes targeted weight edits to fix looping reasoning in small language models, lifting Qwen3.5-2B GSM8K accuracy from 21.6% to 69.4% in one setting; one subproblem ran on an IBM Heron processor as proof of concept.
